package_info.why_malicious: The report describes a surge in phishing and malware campaigns leveraging COVID-19 themes, but does not mention any specific malicious software package, code, or library. The threats are primarily social engineering attacks (phishing emails) rather than malicious code distributed via software packages.

behavioral_signatures: Phishing emails using COVID-19 lures or impersonating government/health organizations
Emails prompting users to download suspicious attachments or click on malicious links
Use of pandemic-related urgency or fear to manipulate recipients
file_indicators: Email attachments with generic or COVID-19-themed filenames (e.g., COVID19-update.pdf, WHO-guidelines.docx)
Links to domains mimicking health organizations or government agencies
network_indicators: Outbound connections to newly registered or suspicious domains themed around COVID-19
Links to phishing sites impersonating WHO, CDC, or government portals
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor inbound email for COVID-19-themed subject lines, attachments, or links, especially those impersonating trusted organizations. Use sandboxing to analyze attachments and URLs. Flag emails with mismatched sender domains or those requesting sensitive information. Employ threat intelligence feeds to block known phishing domains and update detection rules for pandemic-related lures.
